rows.description: A boy in class gives me a small gift and keeps looking at me. If I am not comfortable, I say a polite no, thank you. Being clear and kind is right, and I can tell a trusted adult if he keeps pushing.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, mockery, rejection, respect, rivalry, shame

rows.description: My friend tells me a secret and I feel special and responsible. Keeping it shows I am trustworthy. A wise friend keeps it unless someone could be hurt, then tells a trusted adult and explains why.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, coercion, curiosity, gratitude, guilt, temptation

rows.description: The secret is so juicy and I want to tell one other person. I remind myself trust is fragile and a betrayal cannot be undone. If I keep it, I grow trustworthy. If I slip, I own up and apologise.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, coercion, curiosity, gratitude, guilt, trust

rows.description: I told my best friend a secret and now everyone knows. I feel hot and hurt. Wise: tell her how it felt and decide how much to trust her later. It is fine to be careful, but not to be cruel back.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, curiosity, gratitude, guilt, temptation, trust

rows.description: My friend told me she is being hurt at home and I do not know what to do. This is too big for me to carry alone. Telling a trusted adult like a teacher is loving, not disloyal. I explain that to her gently.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, coercion, curiosity, gratitude, guilt, temptation

rows.description: I let out a secret in a fight and now feel awful. Honesty is best: say sorry, no excuses, and accept that trust may take time. Blaming her for making me angry hides my responsibility.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, coercion, curiosity, gratitude, temptation, trust
related mind states: anger, guilt, trust

rows.description: I keep a secret from my parents because I fear they will be angry. Some privacy is normal, but big worries need sharing. A safe parent reacts calmly. I can start with I need to tell you something, promise not to shout.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, coercion, curiosity, gratitude, guilt, temptation
related mind states: anger, fear, anxiety, calm

rows.description: A classmate says she will be my friend only if I tell her someone's secret. That is manipulation, not friendship. I can say no and walk away, and tell an adult if she keeps pressing.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, coercion, curiosity, gratitude, guilt, temptation

rows.description: An older person says this is our secret and asks me not to tell my parents. Any secret that makes me feel uneasy must be told to a trusted adult. It is never my fault, and telling is brave and right.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, curiosity, gratitude, guilt, temptation, trust

rows.description: I told a friend something private and she kept it and just listened. I feel lighter and closer to her. Good friends prove themselves in small quiet ways, and I can repay that trust.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, coercion, curiosity, guilt, temptation, trust
